The author provides a critical analysis of six research papers published by M.A. El-Hakiem and his co-workers.
The papers were published in International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer, Journal of Magnetism and Magnetic Materials, and Heat and Mass Transfer.

The papers cover topics related to magnetohydrodynamic free convection flow, heat and mass transfer in micropolar and non-Newtonian fluids, and the effects of Joule heating, viscous dissipation, thermal radiation, and lateral mass transfer.
The author identifies that many of the velocity and temperature profiles presented in the six papers do not asymptotically approach the ambient fluid conditions, as expected in boundary layer theory.
Instead, the profiles intersect the line representing the boundary conditions, which is incorrect.
The author suggests that the incorrect profiles are likely due to the use of a small calculation domain, which resulted in the profiles being truncated.
The author provides schematic diagrams to illustrate the correct and incorrect profile shapes.

The incorrect profiles are found in the following papers and figures: 1) First paper: All profiles in Figure 1; 2) Second paper: All profiles in Figures 1 and 4; 3) Third paper: All profiles in Figures 7 and 10; 4) Fourth paper: Some profiles in Figures 2 and 3; 5) Fifth paper: Some profiles in Figure 6; 6) Sixth paper: Some profiles in Figures 3, 5, 6, and 7.
The author is an Associate Professor of Fluid Mechanics at the School of Engineering, Democritus University of Thrace, Greece.
